mainTopic: The two categories בְּהֵמָה (domesticated animal) and חַיָּה (wild animal) include each other in the Torah's language, as רבי ישמעאל taught. The גמרא finds the פסוקים for this and begins explaining what each inclusion is for.
overview: The amud opens at the end of רבי ישמעאל's teaching that in the Torah's language the words בהמה and חיה include each other, and בן עזאי wishes he had served him. The גמרא finds a פסוק for each direction, one in דברים and one in ויקרא. It then explains what each inclusion is used for: the kosher signs, the ban on mating different kinds, רבי's גזירה שוה showing that ויקרא 5:2 is about טומאת קודש, and the laws of a miscarried fetus. That last use follows רבי מאיר in a משנה from נדה; the חכמים say only a human-shaped fetus counts as a birth. The גמרא then explains that the רבנן of our משנה use all of ויקרא 5:2 for רבי's teaching. A new משנה rules that a midwife who touches a dead fetus inside its mother becomes טמא for seven days, but the mother stays טהור until the fetus comes out. רבה teaches that swallowed impurity does not make things impure, and swallowed purity cannot become impure. The גמרא proves the first half from someone who ate נבלה just before sunset, and defends the proof for both רבי יוחנן and בר פדא. It then starts a קל וחומר from a sealed clay vessel to prove the second half, which finishes on the next amud.

steps.title: Domesticated and wild animals are counted together, for non-kosher and kosher alike
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל's rule finishes: a non-kosher בהמה falls under non-kosher חיה, and a kosher בהמה falls under kosher חיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A non-kosher domesticated animal is included in the category of a non-kosher wild animal, and a kosher domesticated animal is included in the category of a kosher wild animal.
steps.whatsHappening: We are picking up at the end of רבי ישמעאל's teaching. He says that the Torah's words בהמה and חיה overlap, both for non-kosher animals and for kosher ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that the Torah's word for one type of animal can cover the other type too. So when a פסוק says 'בהמה', it may also be teaching about a חיה, and the other way around. This works the same for טמאה animals and for טהורה animals.

keyTerms.meaning: A domesticated animal, like a cow, sheep or goat
A wild animal, like a deer or gazelle
Included in the category of
Non-kosher
Kosher

steps.confusionAlert: In everyday Hebrew, בהמה and חיה are two separate groups. The whole חידוש here is that the Torah's wording sometimes uses one word to cover both groups.

phrases.english: A non-kosher domesticated animal is included in a non-kosher wild animal,
a kosher domesticated animal is included in a kosher wild animal,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from before this section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the Torah's language, בהמה and חיה include each other, for both kosher and non-kosher animals.

steps.title: בן עזאי wishes he had learned from רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: The speaker of the ברייתא reports that בן עזאי reacted by saying: woe to me that I did not serve רבי ישמעאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in these words he said to me: Woe to בן עזאי, who did not serve רבי ישמעאל!
steps.whatsHappening: After hearing רבי ישמעאל's explanation, בן עזאי shows how much he admires it. He is sorry he never served רבי ישמעאל as a student.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Serving a רבי (שימוש תלמידי חכמים) was the way to absorb his teachings up close. בן עזאי's sigh tells us that רבי ישמעאל's way of reading the פסוקים solved a real problem in a fresh way.

keyTerms.meaning: Woe to, what a loss for
Served (attended a Torah teacher as his student)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי ישמעאל teaches that the words בהמה and חיה overlap in the Torah, and בן עזאי praised it highly.

phrases.english: And in these words he said to me:
phrases.notes: 'He' is בן עזאי, who says this about himself.

phrases.english: Woe to בן עזאי
who did not serve רבי ישמעאל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the ברייתא with בן עזאי's reaction to the teaching
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בן עזאי praises רבי ישמעאל's teaching by regretting that he never served him.

steps.title: Where do we learn that a wild animal is called a domesticated animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the Torah source showing that חיה is included in בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that a wild animal is included in the category of a domesticated animal?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now looks into רבי ישמעאל's rule. First it asks for the פסוק behind the first half: חיה is included in בהמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rule like this cannot just be assumed; it needs a source in the Torah's wording. The גמרא will look for a place where the Torah says 'בהמה' but lists wild animals.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.english: From where do we know that a wild animal is included in domesticated animal?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule taught in the ברייתא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that shows חיה is included in בהמה

steps.title: The Torah lists deer and gazelle under the heading 'בהמה'
steps.stepSummary: In דברים, the list of kosher 'בהמה' includes wild animals like the deer and gazelle, so חיה must be included in בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'These are the בהמה that you may eat: ox, sheep... deer, gazelle, fallow deer...' How can that be? It must be that חיה is included in בהמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק. The heading says 'בהמה', but the list includes wild animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The deer, gazelle and fallow deer are clearly חיות, not tame animals. Yet the Torah puts them under the heading 'זאת הבהמה'. The only way this makes sense is that the word בהמה covers חיה too.

keyTerms.meaning: How can this be? (pointing out something that needs explaining)
Deer, gazelle and fallow deer, which are wild animals
Etc.: the rest of the פסוק

phrases.english: As it is written: 'These are the domesticated animals that you may eat:
an ox, a sheep, etc.
a deer, a gazelle, a fallow deer, etc.'
How can this be?
A wild animal is included in domesticated animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק in דברים lists wild animals under the heading 'בהמה', so חיה is included in בהמה.

steps.title: Where do we learn that a domesticated animal is called a wild animal
steps.stepSummary: Now the גמרא asks for the source of the opposite direction: בהמה included in חיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that a domesticated animal is included in the category of a wild animal?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the second half of רבי ישמעאל's rule. It asks for a source showing that the word חיה also covers בהמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Proving one direction does not automatically prove the other. 'Deer are called בהמה' does not show that 'cows are called חיה'. So a separate source is needed.

phrases.english: From where do we know that a domesticated animal is included in wild animal?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel question for the reverse direction of the rule
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that shows בהמה is included in חיה

steps.title: The Torah says 'these are the חיה' and then speaks of בהמה
steps.stepSummary: In ויקרא, the heading says 'חיה' but goes on to describe 'בהמה', so בהמה must be included in חיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'These are the חיה that you may eat, from all the בהמה on the earth: whatever parts the hoof...' How can that be? It must be that בהמה is included in חיה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק from ויקרא. The פסוק opens with 'חיה' but then speaks about 'בהמה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If חיה only meant wild animals, the פסוק should not go on to talk about 'all the בהמה'. Since it does, the word חיה must cover domesticated animals as well.

keyTerms.meaning: Has a split hoof (one of the kosher signs)

steps.whatToRemember: Two פסוקים, two directions: דברים shows חיה is inside בהמה, and ויקרא shows בהמה is inside חיה.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'These are the wild animals that you may eat,
from all the domesticated animals that are on the earth:
whatever parts the hoof'
How can this be?
A domesticated animal is included in wild animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק in ויקרא says 'חיה' and then describes 'בהמה', so בהמה is included in חיה.

steps.title: Including kosher wild animals under kosher domesticated animals teaches the kosher signs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins explaining what each inclusion is used for. Including חיה טהורה in בהמה טהורה teaches that the kosher signs apply to wild animals too.
steps.simpleTranslation: A kosher wild animal is included in the category of a kosher domesticated animal: this is for the kosher signs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now starts going through what each inclusion teaches in practice. The first one is about the סימנים, the signs that make an animal kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The kosher signs are given in a פסוק about בהמה: chewing the cud and having split hooves. Because חיה is included in בהמה, those same signs decide which wild animals are kosher. This is the first item in a list of practical uses that the גמרא is laying out.

keyTerms.meaning: Signs: here, the signs of a kosher animal (split hooves and chewing the cud)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that רבי ישמעאל's rule is not just about wording. It decides real הלכה, such as which wild animals we may eat.

phrases.english: A kosher wild animal is included in kosher domesticated animal:
for the kosher signs.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַיָּה טְהוֹרָה בִּכְלַל בְּהֵמָה טְהוֹרָה לְסִימָנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from finding the sources to explaining what each inclusion is used for
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because a kosher חיה is included in kosher בהמה, the kosher signs given for בהמה also apply to חיה.

steps.title: Non-kosher wild animals are included in the mating ban
steps.stepSummary: Including חיה טמאה in בהמה טמאה teaches that the ban on mating different species also covers wild animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: A non-kosher wild animal counts as part of 'non-kosher domestic animal.' This matters for the ban on mating two kinds together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps going through what each inclusion is used for. Now it covers non-kosher animals and says this one is for the mating ban.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 dealt with kosher animals. Now the גמרא turns to non-kosher ones. The Torah says not to mate your בהמה with another kind, and because חיה is included in בהמה, the ban covers wild animals too.

keyTerms.meaning: Mating animals; here, mating two different species
A non-kosher wild animal
A non-kosher domestic animal
Forbidden mixing of different kinds

phrases.english: A non-kosher wild animal is included in 'non-kosher domestic animal'
this is for the law of mating.
phrases.notes: The פסוק is ויקרא 19:19: 'Do not let your בהמה mate with a different kind.'

steps.triggerLanguage: חַיָּה טְמֵאָה בִּכְלַל בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה – לְהַרְבָּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as step 7, now applied to non-kosher animals
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban on mating different kinds applies to wild animals as well as domestic ones.

steps.title: Non-kosher domestic animals are included for רבי's teaching
steps.stepSummary: Including בהמה טמאה in חיה טמאה is needed for the teaching of רבי, which comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: A non-kosher domestic animal counts as part of 'non-kosher wild animal.' This matters for the teaching of רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the use of the opposite inclusion. It only points to רבי's teaching here, so this line sets up the ברייתא that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the third item in the four-way list. The fourth, kosher בהמה included in kosher חיה, comes in Step 12 after רבי's teaching. The use here is not a direct law. It is a tool that makes a word in the פסוק extra, and רבי builds on that extra word.

keyTerms.meaning: For what רבי teaches (רבי יהודה הנשיא)

phrases.english: A non-kosher domestic animal is included in 'non-kosher wild animal'
this is for the teaching of Rabbi.
phrases.notes: 'רבי' with no name means רבי יהודה הנשיא. His teaching is quoted right after this.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה בִּכְלַל חַיָּה טְמֵאָה – לְכִדְרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The matching opposite case to step 8
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Including בהמה in חיה is what makes רבי's teaching possible.

steps.title: רבי asks why the verse mentions בהמה at all
steps.stepSummary: Since חיה already includes בהמה, רבי asks why ויקרא 5:2 also says 'בהמה טמאה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי says, I could read the verse with just 'wild animal.' So why does it say 'domestic animal' too?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. In it, רבי points out that the word בהמה in the פסוק looks extra and asks why it is there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ויקרא 5:2 lists touching a dead חיה טמאה and a dead בהמה טמאה. Step 6 taught that בהמה is already inside חיה, so 'חיה' alone would cover both. That makes 'בהמה' an extra word, and an extra word must be there to teach something.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I would read'; that word alone would have been enough
Why was it said? This asks about an extra word

steps.confusionAlert: רבי is not doubting the פסוק. He is showing the word is extra so it can be used for a new lesson.

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi says:
I would read only 'wild animal,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:2. It mentions both a dead חיה טמאה and a dead בהמה טמאה.

phrases.english: so why is 'domestic animal' stated?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the teaching of רבי that step 9 pointed to
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the seemingly extra word בהמה in ויקרא 5:2 comes to teach

steps.title: A גזירה שוה shows the verse is about טומאת קודש
steps.stepSummary: 'בהמה טמאה' appears here and in ויקרא 7:21. Just as that verse is about holy food, this one is too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it says 'non-kosher domestic animal,' and later it also says 'non-kosher domestic animal.' Just as there it is about making holy things impure, so too here it is about making holy things impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי answers his own question. The extra word is used for a גזירה שוה with another פסוק that has the same words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ויקרא 7:21 clearly speaks about a person who is טמא and eats from a קרבן. The matching words 'בהמה טמאה' carry that topic over to ויקרא 5:2. So the sin there is about holy food (קודש) and impurity.

keyTerms.meaning: Linking two פסוקים because they use the same words
Here / there, the two verses being linked
Impurity that involves holy things, like קרבנות

steps.whatToRemember: Including בהמה in חיה makes the word בהמה in ויקרא 5:2 extra. רבי uses it for a גזירה שוה with ויקרא 7:21, which shows the verse is about טומאת קודש.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how an inclusion can matter even with no direct law of its own. It frees up a word in the פסוק so a new lesson can be learned from it.

phrases.english: It says here 'non-kosher domestic animal,'
and it says there 'non-kosher domestic animal.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:21, about a טמא person who eats meat of a שלמים offering.

phrases.english: Just as there it is about impurity involving holy things,
so too here it is about impurity involving holy things.

steps.triggerLanguage: נֶאֶמְרָה כָּאן ״בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה״, וְנֶאֱמַר לְהַלָּן ״בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra 'בהמה' sets up a גזירה שוה with ויקרא 7:21, so ויקרא 5:2 is about טומאת קודש.

steps.title: The last inclusion is for the laws of formation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why the תורה includes a kosher בהמה in the kosher חיה category. It matters for יצירה, the 'forming' of a fetus.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rule that a kosher domestic animal counts as part of 'kosher wild animal' is needed for the laws of formation (a miscarried fetus).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reaches the last item on its list of inclusions and tells us what it is used for. It is setting up a quote from a משנה that will show this rule in action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 7 to 9 explained the earlier inclusions. Now we learn that counting בהמה inside חיה matters for the laws of יצירה. If the word חיה covers בהמה too, then a fetus shaped like a cow or sheep is treated like one shaped like a חיה.

keyTerms.meaning: Formation: the 'forming' of a creature, used here for the laws of a miscarried fetus

phrases.english: A kosher domestic animal is included in the category of kosher wild animal
for the laws of formation,
phrases.notes: This points to the word 'formed' (וַיִּצֶר), used both for people (בראשית 2:7) and for animals (בראשית 2:19).

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּהֵמָה טְהוֹרָה בִּכְלַל חַיָּה טְהוֹרָה, לִיצִירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side discussion of רבי's teaching (steps 10-11), the גמרא goes back to its list and explains the last inclusion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Counting kosher בהמה inside kosher חיה matters for the laws of a miscarried fetus (יצירה).

steps.title: The משנה about a woman who miscarries an animal-shaped fetus
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה in נדה. If a woman miscarries a fetus shaped like a בהמה, a חיה or a bird, רבי מאיר says she keeps the days of a birth: for a boy, for a girl, or for both if the gender is unknown.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: a woman who miscarries something shaped like a domestic animal, wild animal or bird, whether a kosher kind or a non-kosher kind, keeps the days for a boy if it is male. If it is female, she keeps the days for a girl. If no one knows, she keeps the days for both a boy and a girl. This is רבי מאיר's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source showing where 'בהמה is included in חיה' makes a difference. רבי מאיר treats an animal-shaped fetus like a real birth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר learns this from the word 'formed,' which is used for both people and חיה. The משנה also lists בהמה, so the word חיה must include בהמה. That is exactly the inclusion from step 12. If the gender is unknown, she takes on the strict side of both: the longer girl periods for impurity, and the boy's days where those are stricter.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who miscarries
Literally 'she sits': she keeps the days of impurity and purity of a woman who gave birth
Male / female
It is not known (whether the fetus was male or female)

steps.whatToRemember: The inclusion of בהמה in חיה matters for רבי מאיר's ruling that a miscarried animal-shaped fetus is treated like a human birth.
steps.confusionAlert: The משנה is not saying the woman gave birth to a real animal. It means the fetus looked like an animal, and רבי מאיר still counts it as a birth.

phrases.english: As we learned in a משנה: a woman who miscarries
something shaped like a domestic animal, a wild animal, or a bird,
whether non-kosher kinds or kosher kinds,
if it is male, she keeps the days for a male.
phrases.notes: These are the birth days of impurity and purity from ויקרא 12.

phrases.english: If it is female, she keeps the days for a female.
If it is not known, she keeps the days for both a male and a female,
these are the words of רבי מאיר.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: הַמַּפֶּלֶת מִין בְּהֵמָה חַיָּה וָעוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the משנה that shows where the inclusion from step 12 makes a difference.
steps.raayaObject: That including בהמה in חיה has a real use for the laws of יצירה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה נדה 21a: רבי מאיר's ruling about a woman who miscarries an animal-shaped fetus.

steps.title: The חכמים say only a human-shaped fetus counts as a birth
steps.stepSummary: The quoted משנה in נדה ends with the חכמים, who say that a fetus without human form is not considered a ולד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: anything that is not in the form of a person is not a child.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה from נדה. After רבי מאיר's view, it now gives the חכמים's opposing view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר said a fetus shaped like a בהמה, a חיה or a bird still counts as a birth for the days of טומאה and טהרה. The חכמים disagree: only a fetus with צורת אדם counts. So according to them, the woman does not keep the birth days for an animal-shaped fetus.

keyTerms.meaning: the form or shape of a human being
a child or offspring; here, a birth that counts for the laws of a woman who gave birth
it is not a child, so it does not count as a birth

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the גמרא's own conclusion. It is the second half of the משנה being quoted, so it gives the other side of the argument with רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
Anything that is not of human form
is not a child.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה from נדה quoted in Step 13, giving the חכמים's view against רבי מאיר.
steps.raayaObject: That the use of the inclusion for יצירה follows רבי מאיר's view; the חכמים, who count only a human-shaped fetus as a birth, disagree.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in נדה: the argument between רבי מאיר and the חכמים about a fetus shaped like an animal

steps.title: Why do the רבנן need this verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the רבנן learn from ויקרא 5:2, since they do not use it the way רבי יוסי הגלילי does.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the רבנן, why do I need this verse?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the argument in our משנה. It asks what the רבנן do with the verse that רבי יוסי הגלילי used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי used ויקרא 5:2 to show that a dead fetus inside a non-kosher animal is טמא. The רבנן say such a fetus is not טמא. So the verse needs a different job according to them, and the גמרא asks what it is.

keyTerms.meaning: a verse from the תורה
why do I need it? (asking what a verse or word comes to teach)
this

phrases.english: And according to the Rabbis,
why do I need this verse?
phrases.notes: The verse is ויקרא 5:2, which רבי יוסי הגלילי used to say a dead fetus in a non-kosher animal is טמא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side point about the משנה in נדה and goes back to the main argument about the verse.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the רבנן learn from ויקרא 5:2 if they do not learn the טומאה of a fetus from it

steps.title: The whole verse comes for רבי's teaching
steps.stepSummary: According to the רבנן, the entire verse is used for רבי's teaching that it is about holy food.
steps.simpleTranslation: The entire verse comes for the teaching of רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The רבנן use the whole verse for רבי's lesson, so nothing is left over to teach about a fetus.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי learned from the words 'בהמה טמאה' that this verse is about someone who became טמא and then ate holy food or entered the מקדש. If the whole verse is busy with that lesson, the רבנן cannot also learn from it that a fetus is טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: all of it, the whole thing
it is what it comes for

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן use all of ויקרא 5:2 for רבי's lesson about holy food, so they have no source to make a dead fetus inside an animal טמא.

phrases.english: All of it is for that which Rabbi taught;
phrases.notes: This is רבי's teaching from Steps 10–11: the verse is about one who became טמא and ate holy food.

phrases.english: that is what it comes for.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן use the entire verse for רבי's teaching about holy food and the מקדש, so it is not free to teach about a fetus.

steps.title: A midwife who touches a dead fetus inside the mother
steps.stepSummary: New משנה: if a fetus died inside its mother and a midwife reached in and touched it, the midwife is טמא for seven days, but the mother stays טהור until the fetus comes out.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A woman whose fetus died inside her, and the midwife put in her hand and touched it: the midwife is impure with seven-day impurity, and the woman is pure until the child comes out.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules on a dead fetus that is still inside its mother and is touched by a midwife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The midwife touched a dead body directly, so she gets the seven-day טומאה of a dead body. The mother is not made טמא while the fetus is still inside her. That only changes once it comes out.

keyTerms.meaning: our משנה, the start of a new משנה
here: a midwife
seven-day impurity, the טומאה from a dead body
her womb (literally: her insides)

steps.confusionAlert: In this משנה, חַיָּה means a midwife, not a wild animal like in the earlier steps. Same word, different meaning!
steps.whyThisMatters: This continues the same idea as the earlier משנה: what is inside a mother's body is treated differently from what has come out.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A woman whose fetus died inside her womb,
and the midwife stretched out her hand
phrases.notes: Here חַיָּה means a midwife, not an animal.

phrases.english: and touched it:
the midwife is impure with a seven-day impurity,
and the woman is pure
until the child comes out.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁמֵּת וְלָדָהּ בְּתוֹךְ מֵעֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A midwife who touches a dead fetus inside its mother gets seven-day טומאה, but the mother stays טהור until the fetus comes out.

steps.title: רבה's rule: enclosed impurity and enclosed purity
steps.stepSummary: רבה teaches that טומאה בלועה does not make things impure, and in the same way טהרה בלועה cannot become impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה says: Just as an impure thing that is swallowed inside a body does not make anything impure, so too a pure thing that is swallowed inside a body cannot become impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion of the משנה with a two-sided rule from רבה about things hidden inside a body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the mother stays טהור while the dead fetus is still inside her, which fits the idea that enclosed טומאה does not spread. רבה adds the mirror image: a pure item that is enclosed is also shielded and cannot pick up טומאה. For example, a swallowed pure ring stays pure even inside a tent with a corpse.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains and analyzes the משנה
Impurity that is swallowed or enclosed inside a body
A pure item that is swallowed or enclosed inside a body
Makes something else impure / becomes impure itself

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the anchor for the rest of the סוגיא. The next steps try to find a source for it.

phrases.english: Gemara
Rabba says:
Just as an impure item that is swallowed (enclosed in a body)
does not make things impure,
so too a pure item that is swallowed
cannot become impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁטּוּמְאָה בְּלוּעָה אֵינָהּ מְטַמְּאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה of step 17 with a general rule that frames its case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Enclosed impurity does not spread טומאה, and an enclosed pure item cannot receive טומאה.

steps.title: What is the source that swallowed impurity does not spread?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn the first half of רבה's rule, that טומאה בלועה does not make things impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that a swallowed impure item does not make things impure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source for the first half of רבה's rule. This sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה built his second half (enclosed purity) on the first half (enclosed impurity). So the גמרא first wants a solid source for the half he compared to.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this? (a request for a source)

phrases.english: Swallowed impurity, from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the first half of רבה's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A scriptural source that enclosed impurity does not spread טומאה.

steps.title: Proof from someone who eats נבלה close to sunset
steps.stepSummary: The תורה says a person who ate נבלה becomes טהור at evening after washing. That holds even if he ate right before sunset and the meat is still in his stomach, so swallowed impurity must not make him impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And one who eats of its carcass shall wash his clothes.' Aren't we dealing even with a case where he ate close to sunset? And still the תורה calls him pure, even though the meat is still inside him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a פסוק about someone who ate נבלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says this person immerses and is טהור when evening comes. That must include someone who ate just before sunset, whose stomach still holds undigested נבלה. If the swallowed נבלה could make him impure, he could never become טהור at sunset. So swallowed impurity must not be able to make him impure.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that died without proper שחיטה; it is impure
Aren't we dealing with (this case too)? This shows the פסוק covers a certain case
Sunset
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה

phrases.english: As it is written: "And one who eats of its carcass
shall wash his clothes,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:40. The פסוק goes on to say he is impure until evening.

phrases.english: Are we not dealing (even with a case)
where he ate close to sunset,
and the Merciful One says he is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Someone who ate נבלה right before sunset still becomes טהור at sunset, even though the נבלה is inside him. So enclosed impurity does not make him impure.

steps.title: Maybe the swallowed נבלה is just no longer fit for a גר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: maybe the eaten נבלה doesn't make him impure because it is no longer fit for a גר תושב to eat, not because it is swallowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe that case is different, because the swallowed meat is no longer fit to give to a גר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the proof by offering a different reason why the eaten נבלה doesn't make him impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נבלה only counts as נבלה while it is fit to give to a גר תושב, meaning fit for a person to eat. Chewed-up meat in someone's stomach is no longer fit for that. So it may have lost its status as impure נבלה altogether. If so, the case proves nothing about swallowed impurity in general.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps (a pushback offering another explanation)
It is different there
A non-Jewish resident who accepted the basic laws; the תורה allows giving him נבלה
Fit, suitable

phrases.english: But perhaps it is different there,
since it is not fit for a ger.
phrases.notes: Based on דברים 14:21, where the תורה says you may give נבלה to the גר. So נבלה means meat a person could still eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא שָׁאנֵי הָתָם, דְּלָא חַזְיָא לְגֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source of step 20 by offering another explanation.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the נבלה-eater as a source for טומאה בלועה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The eaten meat may not be impure because it lost its נבלה status, being unfit for a גר. Being swallowed may have nothing to do with it.

steps.title: The proof still works according to רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that by רבי יוחנן, נבלה stays impure until even a dog wouldn't eat it. By his view, the swallowed meat is still impure נבלה, and the proof stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well according to רבי יוחנן, who says that both this and that stay impure until the meat is unfit even for a dog. By his view, the proof is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the proof survives the pushback, but only by רבי יוחנן's view. This is setting up the next move: what about those who disagree with him?
steps.deeperAnalysis: By רבי יוחנן, נבלה keeps its impurity as long as a dog would still eat it, even if a person wouldn't. Chewed meat in the stomach is still fit for a dog. So it is still impure נבלה, and the only reason it doesn't make the person impure is that it is swallowed.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well (according to one view), usually followed by a challenge for another view
Until it is unfit even for a dog to eat
Well, fine

steps.confusionAlert: הניחא does not end the discussion. It usually means: this is fine for one view, but what about the other view? Expect a challenge to follow.

phrases.english: This works out according to Rabbi Yochanan, who says:
both this and that,
phrases.notes: "This and that" means making a person impure and making food impure.

phrases.english: until it is unfit for a dog: then it is well.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, דְּאָמַר: אַחַת זוֹ וְאַחַת זוֹ, עַד לְכֶלֶב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the pushback of step 21 by one view, and sets up a coming challenge for the opposing view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the answer to one opinion (רבי יוחנן)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The swallowed נבלה lost its impurity because it is unfit for a גר, so the proof fails.
steps.terutzMaskana: By רבי יוחנן, נבלה stays impure until it is unfit for a dog. The swallowed meat is still impure, so the proof shows that swallowed impurity doesn't spread.

steps.title: Does the proof still work according to בר פדא?
steps.stepSummary: According to בר פדא, the stronger impurity of נבלה lasts only while a גר could eat it. So maybe the swallowed meat is no longer impure for that reason, and the proof falls apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to בר פדא, who says: severe impurity lasts while it is fit for a גר, and light impurity lasts until it is unfit for a dog. By him, the reason the swallowed meat does not make the person impure is that it is no longer fit for a גר!
steps.whatsHappening: The proof worked according to רבי יוחנן. Now the גמרא asks whether it also works according to בר פדא, who holds a stricter limit on when נבלה stays seriously impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בר פדא splits the impurity of נבלה into two levels. The severe level stops once a גר תושב would no longer eat it. Swallowed meat seems unfit for a person to eat, so by בר פדא the severe impurity may already be gone. Then the swallowing is not what saves the person, and the proof from Step 20 fails.

keyTerms.meaning: The severe level of impurity of a נבלה
The lighter level of impurity of a נבלה
Here, a גר תושב: a non-Jew living in ארץ ישראל who is allowed to eat נבלה. He is the measure of whether it still counts as 'food'
It is not fit (to be eaten)

phrases.english: But according to בר פדא, who says:
severe impurity lasts while it is fit for a גר,
and light impurity lasts until it is unfit for a dog –
then the reason is that it is not fit for a גר!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 22 saved the proof according to רבי יוחנן. This step asks about the other view, בר פדא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof from נבלה in the stomach (Step 20)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By בר פדא, the severe impurity ends once the meat is unfit for a גר. Swallowed meat seems unfit, so its lack of impurity proves nothing about swallowing.

steps.title: Swallowed food is still fit if you did not see it swallowed
steps.stepSummary: Swallowed meat is only disgusting to someone who watched it being eaten. A person who did not see it could still eat it, so it still counts as fit for a גר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, it is not fit for someone who saw it eaten. But for someone who did not see it, it is certainly still fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge and shows that the proof works even according to בר פדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The meat itself has not changed into something no one would eat. Only the person who knows it was swallowed is disgusted. Since someone who did not know could still eat it, it is still 'food' for a גר. So the severe impurity is still there, and the proof stands again: the only reason the person is not impure is that the meat is swallowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / let us admit
In his presence (he saw it happen)
Not in his presence (he did not see it)

steps.whatToRemember: The source for טומאה בלועה stands for both רבי יוחנן and בר פדא: a person with impure נבלה in his stomach becomes טהור at evening, so swallowed impurity does not make him impure.

phrases.english: Granted it is not fit for someone who saw it eaten,
but for someone who did not see, it is certainly still fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from בר פדא in Step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing what 'unfit' means: being disgusting to someone who knows is not the same as being truly unfit.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Swallowed meat is unfit for a גר, so by בר פדא its severe impurity is gone.
steps.terutzMaskana: Swallowed meat is still fit for someone who did not see it eaten, so its severe impurity remains and the proof holds.

steps.title: Where do we learn that swallowed purity cannot become impure?
steps.stepSummary: Having found a source for the first half of רבה's rule, the גמרא asks for a source for the second half.
steps.simpleTranslation: We have found a source that swallowed impurity does not make things impure. From where do we learn that something pure that is swallowed cannot become impure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second half of רבה's rule from Step 18 and asks for its source. It is setting up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half was about something impure hidden inside a body. The second half is the opposite: something pure hidden inside a body, touched by impurity from outside. A source for one half does not cover the other, so the גמרא needs a new proof.

keyTerms.meaning: A pure item that is swallowed or hidden inside something else
We have found (a source)
From where do we know?

phrases.english: We have found a source for swallowed impurity;
swallowed purity, from where do we know it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁכְּחַן טוּמְאָה בְּלוּעָה, טׇהֳרָה בְּלוּעָה מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first half of רבה's rule now has a source, so the גמרא turns to the second half.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that a pure item swallowed or hidden inside something cannot become impure.

steps.title: Starting a קל וחומר from a sealed clay vessel
steps.stepSummary: A sealed clay vessel does not hold in the impurity inside it, yet it does protect pure things inside it. The גמרא begins to build a קל וחומר from this, pausing to explain why impurity escapes the vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: A קל וחומר: a clay vessel closed with a tight seal does not stop the impurity inside it from spreading out. As the Master said: impurity squeezed into a tight space breaks through and rises all the way to the sky. Yet that same vessel does protect the pure things inside it from becoming impure...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins answering with a קל וחומר based on a sealed clay vessel. In the middle it stops for a short side explanation, and the conclusion of the argument comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Start with what we know: a sealed clay vessel does not hold impurity in, because impurity in a tight space bursts outward. Still, the same vessel keeps the pure things inside it safe. A body is stronger, since step 20 showed it does hold swallowed impurity in. So the גמרא will argue that a body should surely protect swallowed purity.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a weaker case to a stronger one: if it is true there, all the more so here
A clay (earthenware) vessel
A tightly sealed cover
Protects / saves (from impurity)
Impurity squeezed into a tight space with no open air around it
Breaks through and rises upward

steps.confusionAlert: The line starting דְּאָמַר מָר is a side remark explaining why the sealed vessel cannot hold impurity in. The main קל וחומר picks up again at מַצִּיל עַל טׇהֳרָה and is not finished yet.

phrases.english: It is a קל וחומר: if a clay vessel
that is closed with a tightly sealed cover,
which does not stop the impurity
inside it from making things impure,
as the Master said: impurity squeezed into a tight space
breaks through and rises up to the sky –
still protects the pure things inside it from becoming impure,

steps.triggerLanguage: קַל וָחוֹמֶר: וּמָה כְּלִי חֶרֶס הַמּוּקָּף צָמִיד פָּתִיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the question in Step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A קל וחומר from a sealed clay vessel, which protects the purity inside it even though it cannot hold impurity in. The conclusion of the argument comes on the next amud.
